name: Kaluki (European and North American)
description: Kaluki (also spelled Kalooki or Kalookie) is a popular rummy variant played throughout Europe and North America. Using two standard decks plus Jokers, players aim to meld all their cards through sets and runs. The defining feature is the initial meld requirementâ€”typically 40 or 51 pointsâ€”which must be met before a player can lay down any cards. The game rewards careful hand management and the strategic use of Jokers.

history.origins: Kaluki emerged in the mid-20th century as an evolution of standard rummy games, likely developing simultaneously in British and North American card clubs. The name 'Kalooki' may derive from Eastern European Jewish communities who popularized the game in London and New York.
timeline: 1940s: Two-deck rummy variants gain popularity in US and Europe
1950s: 'Kalooki 51' becomes standardized in UK bridge and card clubs
1960s: British and North American rules diverge slightly in melding requirements
1990s: Online gaming platforms popularize Kaluki globally
Present: A staple in European and North American card clubs, especially popular in Jewish communities
history.cultural: Kaluki is particularly associated with Jewish communities in London and New York, where it became a social institution in card clubs. The game is known for being 'polite' but intensely competitive, often played alongside bridge.
history.evolution: The game developed from standard rummy by adding the initial meld threshold (40 or 51 points) and Joker exchange mechanics. British versions typically use 40-point openings while North American versions favor 51 points.

setup.deck: Two standard 52-card decks plus 2 Jokers (106 cards total). Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2 with Aces high only.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 cards dealt singly. The next card is turned face-up to start the discard pile; remaining cards form the stock.
setup.equipment: Standard cards, score sheet, chips or counters for stakes (optional)

rules.objective: Be the first player to meld all 13 cards in your hand by forming sets and runs. The winner 'calls up' and scores zero; other players score penalty points for remaining cards.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Drawing**: Each turn, draw either the top card of the stock or the top discard. 2. **Melding**: If you can form valid melds meeting the initial point requirement, lay them face-up. 3. **Building**: After initial meld, add cards to any existing meld (yours or opponents'). 4. **Discarding**: End turn by discarding one card face-up.
keyRules: Initial meld must total at least 40 or 51 points (house rule)
Sets: 3-4 cards of same rank, all different suits (no duplicates)
Runs: 3+ consecutive cards of same suit; Aces are high only (A-K-Q valid, 3-2-A invalid)
Jokers are wild and can substitute any card in a meld
Jokers in hand at end of play count as 15 penalty points
Building: After initial meld, add cards to extend existing melds on table
Cannot build more than 2 cards to same end of a run in one turn

strategy.basic: Prioritize reaching the initial meld threshold (40/51 points) as quickly as possible. Use high-value cards (Aces, Face cards) to meet this requirement efficiently.
strategy.intermediate: Joker Management: Hold Jokers until you can use them in a meldâ€”15 penalty points is severe. Watch for opportunities to exchange for Jokers on the table. Track which cards have been discarded to calculate drawing odds.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Discarding: Avoid discarding cards that could help opponents complete their initial meld or extend their existing melds. The 'Late Meld' strategy: Hold back small melds to prevent opponents from building on them. Calculate exactly when to 'call up' based on opponent hand sizes.
tips: Three Aces = 33 pointsâ€”more than half the 51-point requirement
Don't hold Jokers too longâ€”the 15-point penalty can eliminate you
Watch opponent discards to deduce what suits they are collecting
In sets with Jokers, you need both missing suits to exchangeâ€”plan accordingly

variations.name: Kalooki 40 (British)
variations.description: Initial meld requirement is 40 points instead of 51. More common in British clubs and faster-paced.

scoring.description: The winner of each hand scores zero penalty points. All other players add up the point value of cards remaining in their hands.
scoring.winCondition: Game continues until all but one player have been eliminated by exceeding 150 penalty points. The last surviving player wins the pool.
